reels.caption: Spending doesn't always mean not saving.

segs: Begin buying back your time the moment your income starts growing as your quality of life gets better, because this was a mistake that took me way too long to realize.
And the sooner you do this, the quicker you'll stop trading time for money and begin selling value instead.
Throughout my life, I've been frugal and I'll save every penny whenever possible, just buying the things when I really have to.
Well, it turns out that's the thing that's stopping you from becoming more than just an employee.
I'll give you a real example.
When I needed to go to client meetings, I used to ride hailing and order motorcycles instead of car rides that ended up costing like 50,000 rupees more.
It was hot, I sweat, and smelled like pollution smoke the moment I arrived in the client's office.
Now compare that to paying the 50K.
I was more comfortable, presentable, arrived in a better state.
And the best part, I could review and rehearse my presentation on the road and arrive more confident.
All of these combined significantly increased my chance to close a deal worth more than 50K.
And now that you see this, it's a logical trade any time of the day.

And look, I'm not telling you to splurge, but you know, these small decisions where you're left hanging and stuck on deciding, I'm telling you there are things like convenience, comfort, state of mind that indirectly translates to money, but are not so obvious to your eyes because it's not that straightforward.
Another example would be investing in how you dress and look, or maybe instead of cleaning your house, just pay someone to do it.
Instead of cooking and doing your dishes, get a catering service, and use the time you save to do a high leverage activity that only you can do.
For example, creating content, because sometimes you can lose more by saving when your time is worth more than what you're saving on.
